lines.text: Do you know a piece of the Wright brothers' first airplane has flown on Mars?
This is Ingenuity, NASA's Mars helicopter, built from NASA's own 3D model. It weighs just one point eight kilograms.
Under its solar panel, NASA attached a small piece of wing cloth from the nineteen oh three Wright Flyer.
Flying on Mars is brutal. The air there is about a hundred times thinner than on Earth.
That's like air twenty-six kilometres up, higher than any helicopter on Earth has ever flown.
So its blades spin up to two thousand nine hundred times a minute. About ten times faster than on Earth.
Two rotors, one above the other, spinning in opposite directions. Just like the Wright Flyer's two propellers.
Radio signals take minutes to reach Mars, so nobody could fly it live. It flew itself.
April nineteenth, twenty twenty-one. It rose three metres, hovered for about forty seconds, and landed.
The first powered, controlled flight on another world. NASA named the spot Wright Brothers Field.
It was meant to fly five times. It flew seventy-two, until its blades broke in twenty twenty-four.
Ingenuity talked to Earth through its rover. Orbi Transfer tries the direct route first.
Phone to phone, straight across. And if that can't connect, it falls back to storage.
